scope: Reference semantic model and fail-closed test expectations; no backend compiler/runtime claims without stepful exact-head guest execution

ownership: rt take consumes one linear owner; any later borrow/send/read through sender is rejected
rt borrow creates a read-only loan; take or write while borrowed is rejected
rt borrow mut is exclusive; no overlapping read or mutable loans
rt share freezes the shared view; no mutation until all shared views released
no loan, read or write can cross actor retirement or stale generation
loans across await/select are prohibited pending pinned continuation validation
actor_state: state is sealed; no direct external actor field read or write
only handle_state(critical-read ...) or handle_state(critical-write ...) with compatible loan semantics
single writer and concurrent readers, no writer/read overlap
mailbox: admission linearizable; no allocations or successful enqueues on capacity refusal
bounded per-actor message slots and per-tenant byte budget
accepted equals completed + failed_turns + abandoned + queued
stale capability and retired actor send are rejected
shutdown drains already-admitted messages unless a supervisor-recorded fault abandons them
supervision: panic from actor sends supervisor-priority CONTROL notification, never actor-visible catch
raise escaping actor handlers promotes to panic if no recover
throw uses nearest catch, unhandled throw promotes to raise then panic
panicking actor has one recorded failed turn; queued abandonment explicit
healthy tenant continues after neighboring actor failure

evidence_limits: Reference model operations are not AttoLang compiler diagnostics.
New GraalVM worker Native Image stress is a host-side Java implementation until emitted from canonical checked MIR.
Canonical LLVM IR exporter only proves a restricted actor subset once its exact-head executed CI succeeds.
Matching model output cannot certify independent scheduling, hostile tenant sandbox or complete ownership checking.
Epsilon prevents GC collections but does not reclaim managed allocations; measure long-run heap and RSS.
